song.title: Hello, I Am Pip
song.styleBrief: children's classroom hello song, 104 bpm, C major, bright and playful; one warm clear female lead with an American accent, every word slowly and clearly sung, no vibrato; call-and-response chorus with a small group of children echoing; acoustic guitar, ukulele in the chorus, glockenspiel melody, hand claps on two and four, soft upright bass; dry, uncluttered, the words lead.
song.lyricSheet:
[intro]
[verse]
Hello, hello, I am Pip
Hello, hello, I am Nan
Wave your hand and say it too
Hello, I am you
[chorus]
Hello, I am Pip (clap clap)
Hello, I am Nan (clap clap)
Hello, I am, hello, I am
Hello, who are you?
[verse]
Point to me, I am Pip
Point to you, you are Nan
Nod your head and say it too
Hello, I am you
[chorus]
Hello, I am Pip (clap clap)
Hello, I am Nan (clap clap)
Hello, I am, hello, I am
Hello, who are you?
[outro]

teacherActions: Hold up one picture card at a time and say the word slowly.
Stretch the first sound: nnnest.
Mix n words with other words.
When the script says nnn, say the sound. When it says "the letter n", say the letter name.
teacherLanguage: "Listen. Nnnest. Nest."
"Is the first sound nnn? Thumbs up or thumbs down?"
"Yes! Nnnest starts with nnn."
"Listen. Cat. Does cat start with nnn? No!"
studentActions: Children say each word after the teacher.
Children show thumbs up for an n word and thumbs down for other words.
watchFor: Children who copy a friend's thumbs: ask them alone with one more card.
Children who say "nuh": the sound is n, with no "uh" at the end.

easier.en: Use only three cards (nest, nose, cat) and say the first sound two times.

harder.en: Ask about the last sound too: "Sun. Does sun end with nnn?"

group.en: Pairs: you hold up a card; partner A says the word, and partner B shows the thumbs.

materials: picture cards: nose, cat, sun, dog, bus
sound picture cards: nest, net, nut

teacherActions: Show the n sound card and point to the letter.
Say the pure sound: lips a little apart, the tip of the tongue on the bump behind the top teeth, voice on, air out through the nose. It is the Thai sound น with no vowel after it.
Do the action of n: nod your head slowly, as for "yes", and hum nnn.
teacherLanguage: "Look. This is the letter n. It says nnn."
"Listen: nnn. Not 'nuh'. Nnn."
"Watch me: nnn. Nod, nod, nod."
"Your turn. Say it and do it. Three times."
studentActions: Children say nnn and nod their heads slowly, three times.
Children point to the letter n on the card.
watchFor: A pure sound: no "uh" at the end.
Every child does the action, not only the front rows.

easier.en: Children put one finger on the nose and feel the hum while they say nnn.

harder.en: Show the n, m, and s cards in a mixed order. Children do the n action only for n.

group.en: Two halves: one half says the sound, and the other half does the action. Then the halves change.

teacherActions: Write a big n on the board and say the formation words while you write.
Write n in the air with your back to the class, so your hand moves the same way as theirs.
Children write n in the air, then trace it in the book three times.
teacherLanguage: "Start at the top. Down. Up. Over the hill. Down."
"Fingers up. Write n in the air with me."
"Open your book. Find the n. Trace it three times. Start at the dot."
studentActions: Children write n in the air with one finger and say the formation words.
Children trace n three times in the book, from the dot.
watchFor: Children who start at the bottom: take their hand and start at the dot.
Children who write a big N: show the small n on the card.

easier.en: Children trace the n in the book with a finger first. Then they trace it with the pencil.

harder.en: Write n two more times on the empty line, with no dots.

group.en: Pairs: partner A writes n on partner B's back with a finger; partner B says nnn.

teacherActions: Keep the picture cards net, nut, and nose face down.
Say the three sounds of a word with a short stop between them, then say them fast. Hold the n: nnn.
Show the picture after the class says the word.
Say the sounds, not the letter names: e as in "egg", u as in "up", o as in "go", t with no "uh" after it.
teacherLanguage: "Listen. Nnn - e - t. What is the word?"
"Say it fast: net!"
"Look. A net. Yes!"
"Next one. Nnn - u - t."
"Last one. Nnn - o - zzz."
studentActions: Children listen to the three sounds and say the word.
Children clap once for each sound, then say the word.
watchFor: Children who say only the first sound: say the three sounds again, closer together.
This week the blending is by ear only; the letters come in the next weeks.

easier.en: Say the sounds closer together: nnne-t.

harder.en: Say a word; children say its three sounds: "Nut." "Nnn - u - t."

group.en: Pairs: partner A says the word, partner B points to the picture.

teacherActions: Put the n card on the word wall: it is the first card of the year.
Ask whose name starts with n. Those children stand and say their name.
teacherLanguage: "This is our word wall. Here is the letter n. It says nnn."
"Whose name starts with nnn? Stand up!"
"Every week, we put new words here."
studentActions: Children say nnn at the wall.
Children with an n name stand up and say their name.
watchFor: Children who stand for a name with another first sound: say both names slowly and compare the first sounds.

easier.en: Point to the n card and say nnn together two times.

harder.en: Children say a word for the wall that starts with n: nose, nest, nine.

group.en: Whole class: the children with an n name lead the sound.

teacherActions: Show the cards a, and, can, one at a time.
Read the word. Show the part that the class cannot sound out yet (all of it except n).
Spell each word with letter names, then write it in the air.
Say the word a short and soft, as in "a cat" ("uh"). Do not say the letter name "ay".
teacherLanguage: "This word is a. A cat. A nest."
"This word is and. Pat and May."
"This word is can. I can jump!"
"This is a tricky word. We remember it. Say it with me."
studentActions: Children read each card three times: loud, quiet, loud.
Children find the n in "and" and "can".
Children write "a" in the air.
watchFor: Children who read "and" as "an": point to the d and read it again.

easier.en: Teach "a" and "and" today; "can" comes on the review strip tomorrow.

harder.en: Children say a sentence with "can": "I can jump."

group.en: Pairs: you show a card; partner A reads it to partner B. Then the partners change.

materials: tricky word cards: a, and, can

teacherActions: Open the practice sheet in the book and point to each line once.
teacherLanguage: "Look at the page. Read the sounds with me: nnn, nnn, nnn."
"A nest. A net."
"Find the word and. Point!"
studentActions: Children read the line of n and point to the tricky word "and".
watchFor: Children who look at the wrong line: show the picture at the start of the line.

easier.en: Read only the line of n.

harder.en: Children read "A nest. A net." alone.

group.en: Pairs point to the lines for each other.

teacherActions: Before day 2, tear the week 1 home card out of each student book. Put the cards in the bags at home time, or give them to the homeroom teacher.
Read the Thai line on the card to the class.
teacherLanguage: "This is your home card. Take it home."
"Show it to your family. Sing the song at home!"
studentActions: Children put the home card in their bag.
watchFor: Children who leave the card on the table: check the bags at home time.

easier.en: Put the card in the bag for the child.

harder.en: A child shows the card to a friend and says: "Nnn, nnn, nnn. Hello, I am ___."

group.en: The line leader gives out the cards.

teacherActions: Show each picture card and say the word two times.
Put the cards on the board. Point to a card; the class says the word.
Ask "Is it a boy or a girl?" for the boy and girl cards.
teacherLanguage: "Look. A boy. Say it: boy."
"Look. Is it a boy or a girl? It is a girl."
"What do we say in the morning? Hello!"
"What do we say at home time? Goodbye!"
"Point to the teacher card!"
studentActions: Children say each word two times after the teacher.
Children point to the card that the teacher says.
Children wave for hello and for goodbye.
watchFor: Children who mix up boy and girl: say both words again with your hand on each card.

easier.en: Use four cards: hello, goodbye, boy, girl.

harder.en: A child points to the boy or girl card and asks the class: "Is it a boy or a girl?"

group.en: Pairs: partner A points to a card, partner B says the word.

materials: picture cards: hello, goodbye, boy, girl, friend, teacher

teacherActions: Show the cover and pages 1 to 7 of "Hello!". Cover the words with your hand. Keep page 8 for later.
Ask what the children can see. They can answer in Thai; you say it in English.
teacherLanguage: "Look at the cover. What can you see?"
"A boy. He is waving."
"Who is this? It is a teacher."
"Look at the bag! What is in the bag?"
studentActions: Children say what they can see, in Thai or English.
Children wave when a child in the book waves.
watchFor: Children who answer in Thai: say the English; the child says it after you.
Do not show the last page yet: keep the puppy as a surprise for the reading.

easier.en: Ask yes or no questions: "Is it a girl?"

harder.en: Before you turn the page, ask: "Who is next?"

group.en: Whole class; quiet children tell a partner first, then the class.

teacherActions: Play the audio of "Hello!" once, at 1.0 speed.
Point to the picture while the audio reads the page; turn the page with the audio.
teacherLanguage: "Now listen to the book. Eyes on the pictures."
"Shh. Listen."
studentActions: Children listen and look at the pictures.
Children wave on every "Hello".
watchFor: Children who do not look: hold the book closer to them.

easier.en: Play the audio at 0.75 speed.

harder.en: Stop the audio before the name on a page; the class says the name.

group.en: Whole class.

materials: audio: "Hello!" (QR on the book, or the tablet)

teacherActions: First reading: read each page and point under each word. The class says the page after you.
Second reading: read "Hello, I am" and stop. The class says the name.
teacherLanguage: "My turn: Hello, I am Pat. Your turn!"
"Look at the words. Hello, I am ... ?"
"Read the last page with me: Hello, I am Pip!"
studentActions: Children say each page after the teacher and point in the air.
Children say the name on each page.
watchFor: Children who say the words but do not look: point under each word slowly.
On the last page, let the children laugh, then read it again together.

easier.en: Read pages 1 to 4 and page 8 only.

harder.en: Children read "Hello, I am" alone; you say only the names.

group.en: Half the class reads one page, the other half reads the next.

teacherActions: Write "Hello, I am ___." on the board and point to each word.
Say it with your own name. Then give some children a family card (boy, girl, friend, teacher).
Six children stand, one at a time, and say the frame with their own name. Then all children say it to a partner.
teacherLanguage: "Hello, I am Teacher ___."
"Your turn. Hello, I am ... ?"
"Take a card. Hello, I am a boy!"
"Good job! Say it to your partner."
studentActions: Six children stand, wave, and say "Hello, I am ___." with their own name.
All children stand and say "Hello, I am ___." to a partner, with their own name.
watchFor: Children who say only their name: say "Hello, I am" with them; the child adds the name.
Children who say "I'm": praise it, then ask for "I am", as in the book.

easier.en: The child says "Hello" and the name, together with the teacher.

harder.en: The child adds a second sentence: "Hello, I am May. I am a girl."

group.en: Pairs, then two pairs together: four children say hello to each other.

materials: picture cards: boy, girl, friend, teacher

teacherActions: The whole class acts the book. Say each page; the class says it after you and waves.
On the last page, the class jumps up and says: "Hello, I am Pip!"
teacherLanguage: "Say it with me: Hello, I am Pat!"
"Everybody is Pip. Jump up! Hello, I am Pip!"
studentActions: The class says each page and waves. On the last page, the children jump up.
watchFor: Children who only watch: wave with them and say the name together.

easier.en: The class says only the names; you say "Hello, I am".

harder.en: Children act the book with their own names.

group.en: Whole class.

teacherActions: In the opening, play the karaoke video as the song of the week (item 3). The words are on the screen.
teacherLanguage: "Sing with the words on the screen. Point to the words!"
studentActions: Children sing and point to the words on the screen.
watchFor: Children who only watch: give them the gesture to do (wave, clap).

easier.en: Sing only the chorus.

harder.en: Children sing the verse without the video.

group.en: Whole class.

teacherActions: Show the n card fast, hide it, and show it again.
Children say the sound and do the action.
teacherLanguage: "What sound? Nnn!"
"Again, faster!"
studentActions: Children say nnn and nod their heads slowly.
watchFor: A pure sound with no "uh".

easier.en: Say the sound with the class two times before the fast round.

harder.en: Mix the n card with the m and s cards. Children say the sound only for n.

group.en: Whole class.

teacherActions: Each child has a workmat and an n letter card.
Say a word. Children push the n card into the first box if the word starts with n, and leave the box empty if not.
Four words: nest, cat, nose, dog.
teacherLanguage: "Listen: nest. Nnnest. Is the first sound nnn?"
"Yes? Push the n card into the first box. Say nnn."
"Listen: cat. Is the first sound nnn? No. Leave the box empty."
studentActions: Children listen, push the n card for an n word, and say the sound.
watchFor: Children who push the card for every word: say the word again and stretch the first sound.

easier.en: Use only the words nest and cat, two times each.

harder.en: Add a word with n at the end (sun): children push the card into the last box.

group.en: Pairs share one workmat and take turns to push the card.

teacherActions: Say the sound n; children say it, then write the letter in the book.
Do it three times. Then children trace "a" on the line.
teacherLanguage: "When I say nnn, you write the letter. Ready? Nnn."
"Listen: nnn. Write it again. Start at the top."
"Now trace the word a. Start at the dot. Round, up, down."
studentActions: Children say the sound and write n three times in the book.
Children trace the tricky word "a".
watchFor: Children who write n from the bottom: show the start dot again.

easier.en: Children trace n before they write it.

harder.en: Children write n with their eyes closed, then check it.

group.en: Pairs check each other's n: start at the top, down, up, over the hill, down.

teacherActions: Show the cover of "Nan Can Nod". Read the title and ask what the book is about.
Read page 1 with the class: point to "A" (a tricky word) and to the n at the start of the picture word.
Then pairs read: partner A reads a page, partner B reads the next.
teacherLanguage: "Look. Nan Can Nod. What can Nan do?"
"Point to the n. Nnnest. A nest!"
"Your turn with your partner. A reads, B reads, A reads."
studentActions: Children read each page: "A" and the picture word with n.
Pairs take turns, page by page.
watchFor: Children who name the picture with a different word (bird for nest): point to the n and stretch the first sound.
This book is a sound book. The child reads "a", then uses the first sound, nnn, to say the picture word.

easier.en: The child reads with the teacher, page by page.

harder.en: The child reads the last page alone: "Nan can nod!"

group.en: Pairs; the teacher sits with one pair.

materials: decodable "Nan Can Nod" (class set, one for each pair)

teacherActions: Ask two questions about the book. Children answer with a short sentence.
teacherLanguage: "Look at page 2. Is it a nut? No! It is a net."
"Who can nod? Nan can nod!"
studentActions: Children answer "Yes" or "No", then the full sentence with the teacher.
watchFor: Children who answer only "yes": say the full sentence; the child says it after you.

easier.en: Ask only yes or no questions.

harder.en: A child asks a question about a page: "Is it a nut?"

group.en: Pairs ask each other one question.

teacherActions: Give each child the sticker of "Nan Can Nod".
Children put it on number 1 of the book map in their book.
teacherLanguage: "You read the book! Here is your sticker."
"Put it on the book map, on number 1."
studentActions: Children put the sticker on the book map and say the book title.
watchFor: Children who put the sticker in the wrong place: show number 1 on the map.

easier.en: Put the sticker on the map with the child.

harder.en: The child says the title and one word from the book.

group.en: The table leader gives out the stickers.

teacherActions: Ask two or three children to read their favorite page of "Nan Can Nod".
teacherLanguage: "Which page do you like? Read it to us."
studentActions: Two or three children read one page each.
watchFor: Children who are not sure: let them choose a page, then read it with them.

easier.en: The child points to the page; the class reads it.

harder.en: The child reads the page and says why: "I like Pip!"

group.en: Whole class.

teacherActions: Children read "Nan Can Nod" again in pairs, with a finger under the words. Partner A reads a page, partner B reads the next.
Sit with one table and listen to each child read two pages.
teacherLanguage: "Read the book again. Finger under the words."
"Read page 3 to me. Good! A nut."
studentActions: Children read the book in pairs, with a finger under each word.
watchFor: Note on the record sheet the children who still name the pictures with a different first sound.

easier.en: The child reads together with the partner.

harder.en: The child reads the book two times, the second time faster.

group.en: Pairs; the teacher listens to one table.

teacherActions: Show the cards a, and, can fast.
Write "and" on the board, then erase one letter; children say the missing letter.
teacherLanguage: "Read it fast! And. Can. A."
"Close your eyes. ... Open your eyes. What is missing?"
studentActions: Children read the cards fast.
Children say the missing letter name.
watchFor: Children who say the letter sound for the missing letter: accept it, then say the letter name.

easier.en: Show only "a" and "and".

harder.en: Erase two letters of "can".

group.en: Whole class.

materials: tricky word cards: a, and, can

teacherActions: Give out the class set of "Hello!" (Sprout band).
Read it together once, then pairs read it page by page.
teacherLanguage: "Open your book. Read with me."
"Now read it with your partner. A reads, B reads."
studentActions: Children read "Hello!" together, then in pairs.
watchFor: Children who read a name wrong: point to the picture of the child on the page.

easier.en: Pairs read only pages 1 to 4.

harder.en: The child reads the whole book to the partner.

group.en: Pairs.

materials: reader "Hello!" (class set, one for each pair)

teacherActions: Children trace "Hello, I am" in the book.
Then they copy their name from their name card on the line.
Show where the capital letter and the period go.
Before day 4, write each child's English name on a name card.
teacherLanguage: "Trace the words: Hello, I am."
"Now write your name. Look at your name card."
"A big letter at the start of your name. A period at the end."
"Now draw a picture of you. Wave hello!"
studentActions: Children trace the frame and write their own name.
Children draw themselves waving in the picture box.
watchFor: Children who write the name with no capital letter: point to the big letter on the name card.

easier.en: Write the child's name with a highlighter; the child traces it.

harder.en: The child traces a second line: "I am a boy." or "I am a girl."

group.en: Alone; pairs show each other the page at the end.

teacherActions: Ask four children to read their sentence to the class.
teacherLanguage: "Read your sentence to us. Hold up your book."
studentActions: Four children read "Hello, I am ___." from their book.
watchFor: Children who read too quietly: stand next to them and read with them.

easier.en: The child reads with the teacher.

harder.en: The child reads both lines.

group.en: Whole class; the class waves back.

teacherActions: In the day 5 opening, the song of the week (item 3) is the song show. The class sings with all the gestures; one table leads.
If the school allows it, film the song on the class tablet.
teacherLanguage: "Table 1, you are the leaders today. Show us the actions!"
"Show time! Sing it with all the actions!"
studentActions: The leaders do the gestures in front; the class sings and copies.
watchFor: Leaders who forget a gesture: point to the screen.
Children who are shy on the film: they can stand in the back row.

easier.en: Sing only the chorus with the gestures.

harder.en: The leaders sing the verse alone.

group.en: One table leads each week.

teacherActions: Before the lesson, set up the four centers: sound cards game, letter cards, book corner, and karaoke corner. Use the same places every week. Before day 5, put the children in four groups.
Groups 1 and 2 start at the sound cards and the letter cards; groups 3 and 4 at the book corner and the karaoke corner.
teacherLanguage: "Group 1, go to the sound cards. Group 2, the letter cards."
"Group 3, the book corner. Group 4, the karaoke corner."
studentActions: Children go to their center and sit down.
watchFor: Groups that do not know where to go: point to the group sign at each center.

easier.en: Put a picture of each group on its center.

harder.en: A group leader shows the center card to the group and does the first turn.

group.en: Four groups.

teacherActions: Groups work at their center. Sound cards: sort the picture cards into n and not n. Letter cards: a child turns over a picture card and says the word; the group pushes the n card for an n word. Book corner: read "Hello!" and "Nan Can Nod". Karaoke corner: sing with the karaoke video on the tablet, with the sound low.
Sit at the reading-record table with the first two children on the record sheet list. Each child reads "Nan Can Nod"; mark the record sheet.
In week 1, walk between the centers for the first 3 minutes and show each group its task.
teacherLanguage: "Read the book to me. Finger under the words."
"Good! What sound? Nnn."
studentActions: Children work at the center.
Two children read to the teacher.
watchFor: Note the pictures that each child names with the wrong first sound.

easier.en: At the reading table, the child reads with the teacher.

harder.en: At the reading table, the child also reads page 8 alone.

group.en: Four groups; the teacher with two children.

materials: picture cards: nose, cat, sun, dog, bus (two sets)
sound picture cards: nest, net, nut (two sets)
tablet: karaoke video "Hello, I Am Pip"

teacherActions: Groups change: 1 and 2 go to the book corner and the karaoke corner; 3 and 4 go to the sound cards and the letter cards.
Listen to child 3 and child 4 at the reading-record table.
teacherLanguage: "Change! Group 1, the book corner. Group 2, the karaoke corner. Group 3, the sound cards. Group 4, the letter cards."
"Read the book to me. Finger under the words."
studentActions: Children change centers and work.
Two children read to the teacher.
watchFor: Groups that change slowly: count down from five.

easier.en: Keep the same center for a group that needs more time.

harder.en: Groups that finish early make a new sort with the picture cards.

group.en: Four groups; the teacher with two children.

materials: picture cards: nose, cat, sun, dog, bus (two sets)
sound picture cards: nest, net, nut (two sets)
tablet: karaoke video "Hello, I Am Pip"

teacherActions: Play "Swat the n": put six picture cards on the board.
Say the word of one picture. Two children run to the board. The first child to touch that picture says the word.
teacherLanguage: "Ready? Nose!"
"Touch the picture. Does it start with nnn? Yes! Nnnose."
"Next two. Ready?"
studentActions: Two children at a time touch the picture and say the word.
The class says "Nnn!" for every n word.
watchFor: Fast children who always win: ask them to touch with the left hand, or hop to the board.

easier.en: Put only three picture cards on the board.

harder.en: Say only the first sound; the child finds a picture with that sound.

group.en: Two teams; one child from each team at a time.

materials: sound picture cards: nest, net, nut

teacherActions: Children do the check page: circle the picture that starts with n in each row, and write the letter n.
Collect the books and mark the check.
Say the three picture words of each row: row 2 dog, nose, bus; row 3 hat, cup, net.
teacherLanguage: "Row 1: nest, cat, fish. Which one starts with nnn? Circle it."
"Now write the letter n."
studentActions: Children circle one picture in each row and write n.
watchFor: Children who circle every picture: mark n as weak on the record sheet; it goes back on the review strip.

easier.en: Sit next to the child and point to each picture while you say it.

harder.en: The child writes a second n with no dots.

group.en: Alone.

line.en: This week, your child learns the sound "nnn" (not the letter name "en"), as in "nose". Your child also learns to say "Hello, I am ___." in English.

activity.en: Say "Hello!" to your child in English. Your child answers "Hello, I am ___." with his or her name. Then find three things at home that start with the sound "nnn": for example, a nose, a nut, and a net.
